newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Scotts says no qualification on accounts.
newsitem.headline: Scotts says no qualification on accounts.

text.p: Scotts Holdings' accounts were in proper order and auditors Ernst & Young had not made any qualifications, director Chuen Fah Alain Ahkong said on Monday.
Ahkong was responding to a a shareholder who asked at the company's annual general meeting whether any nasty surprises were in store for the the retail and property company.
Scotts plunged into the red with losses of S$11.32 million for the financial year ended June 30, 1996 compared to a net profit of S$7.09 million in the previous period.
It said in September the losses were due to provisions made for amounts owed by directors' related companies and from its overseas associates.
Shareholders at the AGM were also concerned over the tussle for control among members of the Jumabhoy family, who hold 57.5 percent of the company.
Executive chairman Ameerali Rajabali Jumabhoy and executive director Iqbal Jumabhoy have resigned their positions as a result of the struggle.
Scotts is also engaged in three lawsuits involving Iqbal Jumbahoy and the committee which reported on a troubled land deal in Gurgaon, near the Indian capital of New Delhi.
Ahkong said there were proposals to elect more exective directors to Scott's board there was now only -- Chng Hee Kok, the managing director and chief executive officer.
